To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
p21/wafl and cyclin D 2 are upregulated in HTLV- 1 infected cells and that p21/ waf1 is in a physical complex with cyclinD 2/cdk4 and is not inhibitory.
HTLV-1 Tax upregulates cyclin D2, which in turn upregulates p21/waf. p21/waf then sequesters away from the cyclins E/cdk2 complexes and binds to cyclin D/cdk4.
HTLV-1 Tax upregulates p21/waf and cyclin D, both of which form a complex in HTLV infected cells that is not an inhibiting complex, but rather an activating complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of the human T-cell leukemia/lymphotropic virus type I (HTLV- I) Tax protein.
understanding how HTLV-1 deregulates the G1/S cell cycle checkpoint and how this deregulation contributes to viral pathogenesis.
understanding the molecular basis for how RNA tumor viruses, like HTLV-1, manipulate cell cycle checkpoints.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HTLV-1 infection results in a deregulation of the cyclin E-cdk2 and cyclin D-cdk4 complexes.
HTLV-1 infection leads to the formation of a p21/waf/cyclin D/cdk4 complex that is active and phosphorylates Rb, and thus promotes cell cycle progression.
HTLV-1 Tax upregulates cyclin D2, p21/waf-1, and cyclin E, which in turn leads to the formation of the cyclin D/cdk4 complex, which is active in HTLV- 1 infected cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Tax upregulation of cyclin D and p21 is not a paradox but rather a mechanism to push infected cells through the G/S cell cycle checkpoint.
the Tax protein upregulates cyclin D2 which in turn upregulates p21/waf 1. p21/waf-1 is a cell cycle checkpoint protein that is normally inhibitory.
HTLV-1 induces the expression of cyclin D1, D2, and D3, as well as the expression of the checkpoint protein p21/waf, to promote cell cycle progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RNA tumor virus infected cells can utilize cyclin and cdc complexes to their own ends.
p21/wafl is a key regulator of the G1/S transition in HTLV- 1 infected cells, but not in HTLV- uninfected cells.
HTLV-1 infection leads to the upregulation of the G1/S cell cycle checkpoint protein p21/waf 1 and the G1/S cyclin D2 protein, which together may facilitate HTLV-1 immortalization.
